title: How the strength of an earthquake is measured
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What does magnitude mean for an earthquake?
How much bigger is a magnitude 7 than a 6?

explain.say: Scientists measure earthquakes with seismometers, which record how much the ground shakes. From these records they work out the magnitude, one number for the size of the quake.

draw.text: How the strength of an earthquake is measured

explain.say: The scale is not like a ruler. Each step up of one means the shaking waves are 10 times bigger, and about 32 times more energy is released.
So a magnitude 7 releases about 32 times more energy than a 6, and about 1,000 times more than a 5. That is why the curve shoots upward so steeply.
The biggest earthquake ever recorded was magnitude 9.5, in Chile in 1960. Most quakes are small; thousands below magnitude 3 happen every day without anyone noticing.

faq.q: What does magnitude mean for an earthquake?
faq.a: Magnitude is a single number for how much energy an earthquake released at its source. Today scientists use the moment magnitude scale, which grew out of the older Richter scale.

faq.q: How much bigger is a magnitude 7 than a 6?
faq.a: The ground motion is about 10 times bigger, and the energy released is about 32 times more. Two steps, from 5 to 7, means about 1,000 times more energy.
asks: Is a 7 twice as big as a 6?

faq.q: What is the biggest earthquake ever recorded?
faq.a: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile, magnitude 9.5. It caused a tsunami that crossed the Pacific Ocean.

faq.q: What is the difference between magnitude and intensity?
faq.a: Magnitude is the size of the earthquake at its source, one number. Intensity describes how strong the shaking feels and how much damage it does at a particular place, which is usually greater near the epicentre.
asks: Why do people feel the same quake differently?

faq.a: A seismometer has a heavy mass that tends to stay still while the ground and frame move around it. The difference between them is recorded, showing the ground shaking as a wiggly line.

facts: Each whole step on the magnitude scale means about 32 times more energy released.
The largest recorded earthquake was magnitude 9.5, in Chile on 22 May 1960.

quiz.say: About how much more energy does a magnitude 6 earthquake release than a magnitude 5?
quiz.why: Each step of one on the magnitude scale means about 32 times more energy.

wrong.1: The scale is not like a ruler, so one step is far more than double.
wrong.2: A higher magnitude always means more energy.
